newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar shares edge higher in bank-led trade.
newsitem.headline: Qatar shares edge higher in bank-led trade.

text.p: Shares at Qatar's stock exchange advanced in the week to Thursday, continuing a trend started with the opening of the official floor on May 27, brokers said.
The Commercial Bank of Qatar's 17-share index rose by more than a point to 138.51 from 137.43 in the previous week.

The number of deals transacted rose eight percent to 36, but the volume of shares traded and their value declined. Around 24,644 shares changed hands for a total of 2.28 million riyals ($626,000) compared with 34,780 shares for 6.68 million in the previous week, the official Doha Securities Market said.
The market's information officer, Jamal Rihawi, said in terms of value traded banks took the lead with 4,557 shares worth 1.07 million riyals dealt.
Services followed with 13,694 shares worth 738,725 riyals traded. Some 6,390 industrial shares worth 472,160 riyals also changed hands.

Gainers included the Commercial Bank of Qatar (CBQ) which added five riyals to 335 and Qatar Islamic Bank which rose 7.25 riyals to 152.25. Qatar Cement and Qatar Flour Mills jumped 10 riyals each to 310 and 315 respectively and Qatar Industrial Manufacturing Company advanced two riyals to 70.
Qatar Shipping shed a riyal and a half to 46 and Qatar Leisure lost a riyal to 51.
Meanwhile, the bourse has asked companies listed at the exchange to submit their half-yearly results to it by August 15.
"The move is aimed at increasing transparency in the market," said Mazin al-Shakarchi, CBQ's assistant general manager of treasury and investments.
